newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Birch sees no threat to promised 1998 tax cut.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Birch sees no threat to promised 1998 tax cut.

text.p: New Zealand Finance Minister Bill Birch, speaking before a parliamentary committee on Wednesday, said he saw no threat to tax cuts promised for next year.
He said even if September's pension referendum resulted in a "no" vote, further tax cuts would remain a priority.

"I don't see any risks to the tax cuts next year. We have legislated for them. One can with a high level of certainty say these tax cuts will go ahead," he told a finance and expenditure select committee hearing.
Asked about future tax cuts beyond the ones slated for next year, he said, "There will be a strong incentive on the government (to introduce them)".

Asked about the impact of the possible role of a referendum result which does not allow the RSS compulsory superannuation scheme to go ahead, Birch said, "If it is not (a "yes" result) I think the tax cuts (after 1998) will still be a high priority."

In the Retirement Savings Scheme launched in a white paper earlier this week the Treasury made clear it planned to roll out tax cuts "when fiscally sustainable" hand-in-hand with increases in the level of workers' own contributions to their pensions.
